title: 0/1 Knapsack Basic
hints: for each item, there are only two choices: take it or leave it - what does the answer look like if you know the best value achievable with the remaining items and remaining capacity for both choices?
define dp[i][c] as the max value achievable using only the first i items with capacity c
if item i's weight is more than c, you can't take it: dp[i][c] = dp[i-1][c]. otherwise dp[i][c] = max(dp[i-1][c], dp[i-1][c - weight[i]] + value[i])
process items one at a time, filling in dp[c] for every capacity from 0 up to the max - notice each row only depends on the row above it

since row i only needs row i-1, you can collapse the 2D table into a single 1D array of size capacity+1, as long as you iterate capacity from high to low for each item so you don't reuse an item twice
commonMistakes: iterating capacity from low to high in the 1D rolling version, which lets the same item be counted more than once (that's unbounded knapsack, not 0/1)
forgetting the base case dp[0][*] = 0 (no items means no value, regardless of capacity)
comparing weight[i] to capacity using the wrong index after collapsing to 1D, off-by-one on the item loop

content.problemStatement:
You're packing a bag that can hold up to a given weight capacity. You
have a list of items, each with a weight and a value, and each item may
be taken at most once (it's not divisible and there's only one of
each).

**Choose a subset of items whose total weight does not exceed the
capacity that maximizes total value, and return that maximum value.**
notes: capacity is large enough to fit every item
a single item that alone exceeds capacity (it must be skipped)

sampleTestCases.explanation: taking the item of weight 3 (value 4) and the item of weight 4 (value 5) uses all 7 capacity for value 9, which beats every other combination
no capacity means no items can be taken
the capacity is large enough to take every item, so the answer is the sum of all values

optimal.pattern: knapsack (0/1, bottom-up DP over item index and remaining capacity)

bruteForce.approach: try every subset of items (2^n possibilities), check which ones fit within capacity, and track the best total value among those
